faqs.a: The tool's grid is 2×2: two rows and two columns for each matrix. It offers addition, subtraction, multiplication, and the determinant of A.
Yes. Matrix multiplication is not commutative — A×B and B×A usually give different answers, so the order matters.
faqs.q: Is A × B the same as B × A?

faqs.a: The determinant is a single number that describes the matrix. For a 2×2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] it is a×d − b×c. A determinant of zero means the matrix has no inverse.

formula: For 2×2 matrices: A + B adds matching entries. A − B subtracts them. A × B: entry (i, j) = row i of A multiplied by column j of B, added up. Determinant: det([[a, b], [c, d]]) = a×d − b×c.
howTo: Enter the four numbers of Matrix A in the 2×2 grid — the boxes start with 1 on the diagonal and 0 elsewhere.
Enter the four numbers of Matrix B in the second 2×2 grid.
Tap A+B to add, A−B to subtract, A×B to multiply, or det(A) for the determinant of A.
Read the result shown in the result box below the buttons.
Change any number and tap an operation again to recalculate.
intro: The Matrix Calculator adds, subtracts, and multiplies 2×2 matrices, and calculates the determinant of Matrix A.
mistakes: Entering numbers in the wrong cells — row and column order matters in a matrix.
Multiplying matrices entry by entry instead of row-by-column, which gives a wrong product.
Expecting A×B to equal B×A — matrix multiplication is not commutative.
Forgetting that a matrix with determinant zero cannot be inverted.
tips: Double-check the grid before calculating — one misplaced number changes the whole result.
Work through one small example by hand first so you can spot a wrong answer.
For multiplication, remember: rows of A times columns of B, then add.
If det(A) is zero, the matrix has no inverse — that is a useful check in linear algebra problems.
uses: It is used by students to check matrix addition, subtraction, and multiplication homework, and to find determinants quickly while studying linear algebra.
